input.value: JsonNode representing a valid instance according to the schema (e.g., {"name":"John","age":30})

cases.expected: ValidationResult.isValid() == true and no ValidationMessage in result
cases.description: When a non‑null ExecutionContext and a JSON node that conforms to the schema are supplied with validate=true, walk should return a successful ValidationResult with no error messages.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.isValid() == false and at least one ValidationMessage describing the schema violations
cases.description: When the instance does not satisfy the schema constraints, walk should return a ValidationResult marked as invalid and contain appropriate validation messages.

input.value: JsonNode representing any JSON (valid or invalid) – e.g., {"any":"value"}

cases.expected: ValidationResult.isValid() == true and no ValidationMessage, regardless of node content
cases.description: When validate flag is false, walk should skip schema validation and always return a successful ValidationResult.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.isValid() == false and a ValidationMessage indicating that the instance node is missing or null
cases.description: Passing a null JsonNode should cause walk to treat it as an invalid instance and return an appropriate error message.

cases.expected: Throws NullPointerException (or IllegalArgumentException) because ExecutionContext is required
cases.description: The method expects a non‑null ExecutionContext; providing null should result in an exception rather than a ValidationResult.

input.value: ExecutionContext with recursive anchor enabled (e.g., schema.isRecursiveAnchor() == true)

cases.expected: ValidationResult.isValid() == true and no ValidationMessage, confirming that recursive anchors are processed without infinite recursion
cases.description: When the schema defines a recursive anchor, walk must correctly resolve $recursiveRef without stack overflow and validate the node successfully.

input.value: ExecutionContext created via JsonSchema.createExecutionContext() for a schema that is a resource root (schema.isSchemaResourceRoot() == true)
JsonNode representing a valid instance for the resource‑root schema

cases.expected: ValidationResult.isValid() == true, confirming that walk works when the schema is marked as a resource root
cases.description: Ensures that walk correctly handles schemas flagged as resource roots, which may affect resolution of relative $ref URIs.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.isValid() == true; the customizer (if any) is invoked without affecting validation outcome
cases.description: Although the focal overload does not accept a customizer directly, the internal walkAtNodeInternal may receive a null customizer; this test confirms that the default path works and that providing a customizer via the overload that accepts it does not change the result.

input.value: ExecutionContext created via JsonSchema.createExecutionContext() for a schema containing a malformed $ref (e.g., "$ref": "http://[invalid-uri]")

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException (or JsonSchemaException) indicating that the $ref URI is malformed
cases.description: The schema contains a $ref with an invalid URI syntax. walk should detect the malformed reference during resolution and throw an appropriate exception rather than returning a ValidationResult.

input.value: ExecutionContext created via JsonSchema.createExecutionContext() for a schema that contains a $ref to a non‑existent definition (e.g., "$ref": "#/components/schemas/Unknown")

cases.expected: JsonSchemaException (or IllegalArgumentException) stating that the reference could not be resolved
cases.description: When a $ref points to a fragment that does not exist in the schema, walk must fail fast and throw an exception indicating the unresolved reference.

input.value: ExecutionContext with recursive anchor enabled and a recursion depth limit set to a low value (e.g., via ValidationContext#setMaxRecursionDepth(1))

cases.expected: StackOverflowError or JsonSchemaException indicating recursion depth exceeded
cases.description: The schema defines a recursive anchor and the instance references itself. With a low recursion‑depth limit, walk should detect the overflow condition and throw an exception instead of looping indefinitely.

input.value: ExecutionContext instance whose internal ValidationContext is null (constructed manually for the test)

cases.expected: IllegalStateException (or NullPointerException) because the ExecutionContext does not contain a required ValidationContext
cases.description: walk relies on a non‑null ValidationContext inside the ExecutionContext. Supplying an ExecutionContext with a missing ValidationContext should cause an immediate exception.

input.value: ExecutionContext created via JsonSchema.createExecutionContext() for a schema that contains a $ref with percent‑encoded characters requiring an unsupported charset (e.g., "%FF%FE")

cases.description: During $ref fragment decoding, URLDecoder may throw UnsupportedEncodingException for an unknown charset. walk should propagate this as a wrapped JsonSchemaException.
